acceptance.assessment: The final identical frozen cold build is 394.02 seconds versus 428.04 (7.95% lower), and the type/behavior-preserving body edit is 211.50 versus 221.55 seconds (4.54% lower). Their peak process RSS is 2,289,008,640 and 2,303,541,248 bytes, below the respective baseline observations. The fully cached no-op is 6.14 versus 6.15 seconds. The 100/500/2,000-declaration observations are 0.01/0.14/1.89 seconds versus 0.01/0.23/3.47; the largest scaling peak RSS differs by 0.20%, with no material regression. These are single build observations, not statistical speedup estimates. The complete nine-workload, three-sample native gate passes all eighteen unchanged 3x compilation / 2x runtime limits; n-body compilation is 2.934039389264x C. Complete frozen LLVM and native outputs agree for both compiler and manager. All six final native groups passed with real outer exits, and fresh source self-hosting reproduces complete LLVM and native compiler bytes. Acceptance applies to the recorded reproducible O2 native PGO configuration. Ordinary unprofiled R10/R11 construction is not claimed to pass that native gate. The separate current-source cold observation is 549.20 seconds and 3,824,599,040 bytes peak process RSS; it uses ordinary O2 construction with the tested PGO compiler as input and reproduces the ordinary R10 compiler and R11 manager. It is not a frozen-baseline ratio or the profile-use self-host check.
